description: The image displays a set of three pie charts comparing the proportions of four categories across different conditions, with the first two charts explicitly labeled "easy" and "medium," and a third chart with a partially visible label at the top right. A legend on the far right identifies the four categories and their corresponding colors: N+K+ (teal), N-K+ (yellow-tan), N-K- (light orange), and N+K- (dark orange). Each of the three charts contains four slices with percentage labels displayed directly inside them. In the "easy" chart, the slices represent N-K+ at 45.9%, N+K+ at 40.6%, N-K- at 10.1%, and N+K- at 3.3%. The "medium" chart shows N+K+ at 44.6%, N-K+ at 44.3%, N-K- at 7.2%, and N+K- at 3.9%. The third chart displays N-K- at 36.8%, N-K+ at 36.2%, N+K+ at 20.1%, and N+K- at 7.0%. The slices are arranged in a consistent clockwise categorical order across all three charts rather than being sorted by size. None of the slices are visually emphasized, exploded, or offset, and the text "CoT" is visible below the "medium" chart.
